Run an event end to end Preview

This is the operator walkthrough: from a freshly deployed platform to a competitor solving a problem in their own cloud account. It is the prose form of the single-pass flow the platform guarantees (tenant creation → application console → problem deploy → participant join).

Create a tenant

In SaaS mode, a System Admin creates a tenant from the admin-console (the control plane front end). Tenant creation emits onboardingRequest; the tenant is provisioned as pooled by default, or as a dedicated silo stack for the PLATINUM tier. The tenant admin then receives the application-admin-console URL for their plane. In Lite mode there is a single local tenant and you go straight to the application console.

Connect a competitor account

Each competing team deploys a one-time CloudFormation template (infrastructure/templates/competitor-bootstrap.yaml) into their own AWS account. It creates a least-privilege IAM role whose trust policy is pinned to the TenkaCloud control-plane account id and the tenant's ExternalId, so only TenkaCloud — and only for that tenant — can assume it. The team shares the resulting role ARN back to the operator. The full competitor-side steps live in the competitor setup guide.

Deploy a problem

In the application-admin-console, create an event, pick problems from the catalog (the picker only offers cloud-deployable problems — local-only container problems are excluded, and non-AWS problems appear once multi-cloud is enabled), assign each team's account and region, and deploy. Each deploy assumes the team's role with the ExternalId and runs CloudFormation in their account. Watch status by polling the deployment until it reaches a terminal state, then tear it down from the same console when the event ends.

Enable multi-cloud

To run Sakura / Azure / GCP problems, set features: { "nonAwsRuntime": true } in runtime-config.json. A Team Cloud Credentials panel then appears on the Competitor Accounts page; register each team's provider credentials there (the panel writes them to SSM SecureString via the API — operators never touch SSM directly). Once a provider's credentials are registered, that provider's problems become selectable in the event picker. The provider-by-provider credential steps and which fields go in the panel are in the competitor setup guide, and the support state of each runtime is the runtime capability matrix.

Related: deploy modes and launch paths and the platform architecture.
